findings.issue: Both attack rules use hit_count <= 3 without identifying the E activation or empowered attack sequence. This turns the next three attacks after activation into an ordinary attack/hit-count predicate.
findings.shortSourceQuote: Cho'Gath's next 3 Attacks launch spikes
findings.correction: Gate rules[0] and rules[1] on the empowered E attack sequence (activation=empowered). Preserve the next-three-attacks allowance with a count parameter or a retained attack-sequence condition; do not treat it as arbitrary successful hits or global attack count.

findings.issue: Monster percent-health replacement is gated by caster.resource > en:body:n18, whose source value is the unrelated 0.5% Feast damage increase per stack. The source supplies no such resource threshold.
findings.shortSourceQuote: Percent Health damage against monsters is replaced with 80/110/140/170/200.
findings.correction: Remove the resource > 0.5% condition. Keep the monster condition and empowered attack scope. Restrict replacement to the percent-health component, preserving flat base damage and the caster AP component.

findings.issue: The three damage rules are supported, but the explicit on-kill stack and 80/120/160 max-health gain have no corresponding rule or numeric preservation. The summary mentions growth while the gap does not explain why this certain health gain was omitted.
findings.shortSourceQuote: If this kills the target, Cho'Gath gains a stack, which causes him to grow in size and gain 80/120/160 max Health.
findings.correction: Add a rule for this cast killing its own target, with a stack gain, size growth, and caster max-health gain using en:body:n8/n9/n10. Retain the minion/non-epic cap and any range behavior that cannot be typed as text/gaps without inventing formulas.

findings.issue: The rule has only a first-hit predicate on ability_hit; it does not limit the triggering incoming effect to an immobilizing effect. The effect text is correct, but the structured trigger also admits an ordinary first ability hit.
findings.shortSourceQuote: Dr. Mundo resists the first Immobilizing effect that hits him
findings.correction: Add a retained condition specifying that the incoming effect is immobilizing, and identify first within that effect class. Keep the current-health loss as text because currentHealth is unavailable in STATS.

findings.issue: Canister pickup requires caster.activation=visible, a condition absent from every supplied source. This incorrectly suppresses pickup benefits depending on visibility/activation state.
findings.shortSourceQuote: Moving over it reduces this Ability's Cooldown by 15 seconds and restores 4% max Health.
findings.correction: Remove activation=visible. Retain entering/moving over the canister and the supported cooldown reduction and max-health-based heal.

findings.issue: The champion-type condition is attached to target, which the other condition and destruction effect identify as the canister. The source requires the moving enemy to be a champion, not the destroyed object.
findings.shortSourceQuote: Enemy champions moving over the cannister destroy it.
findings.correction: Move target_type=champion to subject enemy, matching trigger.subject=enemy. Keep the canister as the target of the destruction effect.

findings.issue: The damage parameter references target maxHealth even though both source and effect text require target current Health. The frozen STATS enum lacking currentHealth does not authorize substituting maxHealth.
findings.shortSourceQuote: dealing 20/22.5/25/27.5/30% current Health magic damage to the first enemy hit
findings.correction: Remove stat=maxHealth from this coefficient. Retain target current-health scaling in text with stat/statSubject null or an explicit unknown representation, and add an unsupported_formula gap. Preserve the supplied percentages, first-hit condition, minimum damage, and monster cap.

findings.issue: The storage rule is gated only by time > 0.75, leaving no active-W condition or end bound. The first-phase rule also lacks an active-W condition or a declared timer origin. Outside the W duration these predicates can still store incoming damage.
findings.shortSourceQuote: he stores (80% ~ 95%) of damage taken for the first 0.75 seconds and 25% for the remaining duration as gray health
findings.correction: In rules[1] and rules[2], require the W charge to be active and define the timer as elapsed time since that activation. Bound the second phase to the remaining charge duration, ending on recast/expiry. Retain text conditions if the frozen schema cannot represent that state exactly.

findings.issue: Burst damage and both healing branches trigger only on recast. The English summary explicitly supplies duration expiry as another burst trigger; no rule or gap retains it.
findings.shortSourceQuote: At the end of the duration or on Recast, Dr. Mundo deals a burst of damage to nearby enemies.
findings.correction: Add the expiry trigger for the same burst/heal behavior, using the summary only to supplement the trigger and the English body for damage/heal values. Alternatively retain the expiry behavior in an explicit unresolved representation rather than dropping it.

findings.issue: The passive is encoded as a maxHealth-to-totalAttackDamage stat conversion with replace_input and identical percent refs for input/output ratios. The source grants bonus AD based on max health; it neither replaces nor consumes the health stat.
findings.shortSourceQuote: Passive - Dr. Mundo gains bonus Attack Damage, increasing based on his max Health.
findings.correction: Represent this as an additive stat_modifier toward bonusAttackDamage, scaled by caster maxHealth. Remove replace_input and the duplicate output ratio. Preserve the unclear 70%-missing-health passive clause in its existing gap.

findings.issue: A scalar damage_multiplier of 40% represents a fixed multiplier. The source says the additional attack damage is increased by up to 40% depending on missing health, so neither a constant 0.4 multiplier nor a constant 40% increase is supported.
findings.shortSourceQuote: increased by up to 40% based on his missing Health.
findings.correction: Preserve 40% as the upper bound of the additional increase in text/other or unknown-shaped parameters, with the missing-health dependence and an unsupported_formula gap. Do not invent 140% or intermediate values outside the supplied number references.

findings.issue: The path-victim condition is attached to target, but that same target is the enemy killed and swatted away in the preceding rule. The actual damage recipients are secondary_targets. This conflates the corpse with the enemies it passes through.
findings.shortSourceQuote: If the enemy is killed, Mundo swats them away, dealing (5/15/25/35/45 + (5% bonus Health)) physical damage to enemies they pass through.
findings.correction: Retain the primary target being killed by the empowered next attack and swatted away as primary-target context. Attach the path-contact condition to secondary_targets and keep the 5% bonus-health coefficient owned by caster.

findings.issue: The max-health gain parameter scales from caster maxHealth. The source grants max health based on caster missing Health, a different quantity. The gap about whether this is also healing does not justify changing its input stat.
findings.shortSourceQuote: gaining 15/20/25% of his missing Health as max Health
findings.correction: Keep statTo=maxHealth as the gained stat but remove the parameter stat=maxHealth input. Retain missing-health scaling in text with an unknown/null input and an unsupported_formula gap; do not substitute bonusHealth, currentHealth, or maxHealth.

findings.issue: Detonation is gated by target.hit_count >= 3 although the source requires three Blaze stacks. Its own gap states that stack count and hit count are distinct, yet the rule still makes that substitution.
findings.shortSourceQuote: When a champion or large jungle monster reaches 3 stacks
findings.correction: Replace the hit_count guard with a Blaze resource/mark stack threshold using en:body:n5, supplemented by retained text and a gap if necessary. Keep the champion branch and the documented large-monster limitation.

findings.issue: Explosion max-health parameters use statSubject=target even though the scope_ambiguous gap explicitly says the source cannot establish the health owner. This is an unsupported resolution of the ambiguity.
findings.shortSourceQuote: max Health magic damage to surrounding enemies.
findings.correction: Set statSubject=unknown for the explosion max-health parameters and retain the ambiguity gap. Do not select either the original victim or surrounding recipients from background knowledge.

findings.issue: The two seconds before detonation are attached to the damage effect as duration_seconds, while the effect text does not retain the delay. The source describes a delayed burst, not two seconds of explosion damage.
findings.shortSourceQuote: the Blaze will detonate after 2 seconds
findings.correction: Represent two seconds as a delay/time condition or retained delayed-detonation gameplay effect, and state the delay in text. Remove it as a damage duration; preserve the four-second burn duration separately in rules[0].

findings.issue: The damage rule explicitly requires the first enemy hit, but the separately conditional stun rule requires only Ablaze and drops that same first-hit scope.
findings.shortSourceQuote: magic damage to the first enemy hit. If the target is Ablaze, they will be Stunned for 1.75 seconds.
findings.correction: Add target.hit_order=first to the stun rule alongside the Ablaze predicate, so the stun refers to the same first enemy as the damage rule.

findings.issue: Doubled propagation range is typed as movement of nearby_enemies. The source changes the blast spread radius and says nothing about moving those enemies.
findings.shortSourceQuote: If the target is Ablaze, the spread range is doubled.
findings.correction: Use an other gameplay effect on caster/unknown for the ability range change, or another supported range-modifier representation. Retain the doubled spread and primary-target Ablaze condition in text; do not invent a numerical ref for the spelled-out doubling.

findings.issue: The damage effect has scalar count=5 without preserving the can/up-to qualifier in summary or effect text. The source supplies a maximum bounce allowance that can include Brand, not five guaranteed damaging enemy hits.
findings.shortSourceQuote: can bounce to Brand or another enemy up to 5 times
findings.correction: Retain the maximum-five-bounce allowance and possible self bounces in gameplay text/conditions. Keep damage per enemy hit; do not interpret count=5 as five guaranteed enemy damage applications.

findings.issue: The 30/45/60% rank sequence is reduced to a min_amount=30% parameter and max_amount=60% parameter. The middle-rank 45% value is dropped, and per-rank strengths are turned into generic bounds.
findings.shortSourceQuote: If the target is Ablaze, they are briefly Slowed by 30/45/60%.
findings.correction: Use one amount parameter with shape=rank_values and en:body:n5/n6/n7 in order. Preserve the unspecified brief duration as text, without borrowing a duration number.

findings.issue: Bounce targeting priority is encoded as ui_information although it is a stated gameplay selection behavior.
findings.shortSourceQuote: Bounces prioritize stacking Blaze to max on champions.
findings.correction: Retain this as an other gameplay effect describing bounce target priority. Keep the English source priority wording rather than inferring an exact low-stack selection algorithm from the Korean summary.

correctlySupportedNotes.Chogath.P: Enemy-kill health/mana recovery values are correctly retained as level ranges; no interpolation is invented.
correctlySupportedNotes.Chogath.Q: Knock-up duration, ordinary magic damage/AP coefficient, and slow percentage/duration agree with the source.
correctlySupportedNotes.Chogath.W: Silence durations, rank damage values, and caster AP scaling agree with the source.
correctlySupportedNotes.Brand.W: Ordinary and Ablaze replacement damage are separately scoped, and both AP coefficients/rank sequences are correct.

reviewScope: Read-only source semantics review against supplied input sources and the frozen guide/contract. Candidate/code/schema files were not edited. Retained uncertainty or an explicit gap is not by itself an error; reported ambiguity findings identify a contrary concrete assertion.
notes: The documented gap for DrMundo.E passive behavior at 70% missing health and 140% target-type multiplier scope was retained without assuming hidden mechanics.
The documented Brand.P large-monster branch limitation was not flagged merely because its target subtype cannot be expressed by the enum.
Chogath.R damage formulas themselves correctly distinguish champions from minions/monsters and use caster bonusHealth, not baseHealth.
